state.goal: Founder asks: (1) can a shop mark a customer as blacklisted, (2) a Planity-like 'tidy up customers' screen that shows likely duplicates (same name with different emails/phones, different names with the same email, different emails with the same phone) so the shop can group/merge them.

today.blacklist: Does not exist. No flag on customers, nothing stops a booking.
today.customer_model: public.customers is one row per (business_id, email), created by a trigger on every booking insert (ON CONFLICT on exact email). Bookings carry customer_name/email/phone and are linked to customers ONLY by email. 10 tables reference customers.id (notes, loyalty_points UNIQUE(customer_id), loyalty_transactions, customer_gift_cards, gift_cards.purchased_by, no_show_fees, email logs, marketing_sends, receptionist_conversations, consents, outreach_recipients). customer_stats view computes visits/spend live from bookings by lower(email).
today.booking_paths: Public booking widget, AI receptionist/chat, agent API (/agent/v1), and admin-created bookings. Admin bookings must always work.
today.design_rule: Admin lists show status + ONE button that opens a popup; no inline dropdowns or button rows. Owners are often older, use phones, DE/EN/TH.
today.legal: Germany: GDPR. A blocklist is legitimate interest (repeat no-shows, abuse) but must be internal, factual, not shown to the customer, and deletable. Booking history and invoices must never be rewritten (GoBD).

block_effect.instructions: What should happen when a blacklisted customer tries to book?

criteria.refuse_online: Online booking (widget, chat, agent API) is refused with a neutral message 'Online booking is not possible, please contact the shop directly'. Staff can still book them by hand in admin. Staff see a red 'Blocked' badge everywhere.
criteria.require_approval: Online booking goes through but lands as 'needs approval'; shop decides. Customer is not told.
criteria.warn_only: Nothing is stopped; staff only see a warning badge on the customer and their bookings.

block_match.instructions: How is a blocked customer recognised on a new online booking?

criteria.email_or_phone: Blocked if the email (or any email merged into that customer) OR the normalised phone number matches. Harder to dodge with a new email.
criteria.email_only: Only the email matches. Simple but dodged by typing another email.

merge_model.instructions: When the shop merges duplicate customers into one, how should bookings and history follow?

criteria.aliases_no_rewrite: Keep one customer; the other emails are remembered as aliases of it. All linked rows (notes, loyalty, gift cards, consents…) move over; loyalty points add up. Old bookings keep the email they were made with; stats and future bookings match via aliases. Nothing historical is rewritten.
criteria.rewrite_bookings: Rewrite the email on all old bookings to the kept email, then delete the other customer. Simpler queries, but changes historical booking records.
criteria.link_only: Do not merge; only show the customers as a linked group. Stats stay split.

duplicate_rules.instructions: Which customers should the tidy-up screen suggest as possibly the same person?

criteria.three_signals_ranked: Group when they share an email (case/space-insensitive), a phone number (normalised: +49/0, spaces), or a normalised full name. Show WHY (same phone / same email / same name) and rank email/phone matches as 'very likely', name-only as 'check'. Shop can dismiss a group as 'not the same person'.
criteria.strong_only: Only same email or same phone; ignore names (fewer false matches, misses typo-emails).

criteria.customers_tab_with_popup: Customers screen gets a 'Tidy up (N)' button/tab listing suggested groups as rows (names, emails, phones, reason, one 'Review' button). The popup shows the customers side by side, shop picks which name/email/phone to keep, then 'Merge'.
criteria.auto_merge: Merge obvious ones (same email after normalising) automatically, show the rest.
criteria.separate_settings_tool: Put it in Settings › Data tools.
